# Evidence and model lineage in the five oscillator episodes

The five archived episodes support local intervention effects and some
version-specific quantitative transfer. A fresh public-evidence review also
found fitted coefficients being replaced at final submission. Earlier successful
analysis and final predictor accuracy need separate evidence.

The review used partial public exports, inert candidate source and saved-number
arithmetic. No simulator, fit or predictor was executed, and no private scores
or hidden mechanism were inspected. Findings are same-family, provisional and
pending external review; integrity audit unavailable. The five input files remain
unchanged. Historical scores and depth annotations are preserved.

| Public packet | Supported evidence in the export | Final-artifact qualification |
|---|---|---|
| `review-core-001` | Baseline-derived coefficients are tested on interventions and later compositions; three saved numerical contrasts precede fresh matched observations | Prior contrast numbers use a slightly sparse variant; final source restores a tiny AB spring and differs in rounding |
| `review-core-002` | A predicted qualitative AC-cut effect and direct loading/drag contrasts are observed | The only exported fit times out; final coefficients use public-range midpoints |
| `review-core-003` | A late model fits eight baseline preparations near the reported measurement-noise scale | All eight preparations contribute to fitting; final solver changes, with no later observed test in the export |
| `review-core-004` | An earlier heterogeneous model fits baseline/cut/loading/damping data; cuts provide direct edge evidence | Final source replaces every recovered coefficient with range midpoints; the candidate acknowledges loss of fitted constants |
| `review-core-005` | Baseline-derived star connectivity predicts leaf cuts and other interventions using the earlier parameter set | Final grounding and drag arrays change substantially without an established successful returned fit connecting the versions |

## Positive evidence and its exact scope

Packet 001 records three predictions before fresh paired observations. Saved
observed-minus-predicted differences are approximately +0.00127 m/s for a loading
contrast, −0.00294 m/s for a damping contrast and +0.00215 m/s for a cut contrast.
These are replications of previously explored intervention regimes. Later
compound conditions also provide reported coefficient-transfer evidence. The
prior contrasts omit AB; final source restores AB≈0.0000649 N/m. This small
version distinction is not evidence of numerical failure.

Packet 002 observes an AC cut changing A displacement at one second by
approximately −0.09467 m. Under the supplied absent-edge/no-op semantics, this
supports an active AC connection. It does not establish every edge or validate
the final midpoint coefficients.

Packet 005 gives particularly useful star-model evidence: an earlier baseline
fit is used for leaf-cut tests without a further fit, with saved intervention
residuals near the declared noise. The final source subsequently changes every
grounding and drag coefficient. Its three numerical claims select three
channels of one observed AC-cut pair; they are not three independent mechanism
tests. Earlier transfer evidence remains attached to the earlier model.

## Failure modes that should remain visible

Packet 004 replaces the heterogeneous recovered model with common values
`g=1.25`, `c=0.145` and `k=0.725`. Its final short-time claim protocols also differ
from the protocols of cited observations. Those claims may be predictions for
new experiments, but the cited records do not constitute exact matched-pair
replications. Packet 003 explicitly acknowledges lack of intervention
validation; its late near-noise fit is evidence of baseline adequacy rather
than demonstrated transfer.

These are source/provenance findings. They do not independently measure any
final predictor's numerical error or establish that changing a coefficient
necessarily worsened prediction. Export gaps also prevent universal statements
that an unrecorded analysis never happened.

All five public problems supplied the linear force equation, reciprocal spring
family, coefficient ranges and control semantics. Supported scientific claims
therefore concern instance-level structure and intervention behavior within
that family; see [PUBLIC_PRIORS.md](../PUBLIC_PRIORS.md). Inferring a supplied
exclusion, such as absence of nonlinear forces, is not an empirical rival test.

The private structured reviews preserve exact observation/round pointers and
original arrays. Packet 001's central chain is rounds 5→13→14; packet 004's
fitted arrays are in round 4; packet 005's tested estimates and intervention
diagnostics are in rounds 7 and 9. Final source is at
`/final_candidate/submission/predictor_code`. Recorded ordering is not independent
wall-clock authentication. Five hundred and ten pointer, literal and saved-number
checks passed; these are evidence-consistency checks, not new physical tests.

The practical next step is to test persistent candidate-selected model snapshots
and evidence access in a new interface cohort. Every validation should name the
version it actually tested, and final revisions should remain explicit. This
audit does not show that a persistence feature will improve model behavior.
